evidence_test: grep -n 'do_not_enforce_on_create\|enforce_on_create' spec/tohum/*.md spec/asama-0/*.md; grep -n 'create_branch(INTEGRATION' referee/activate.py; grep -n 'create_denied' referee/tests/fake_github.py | head -3  # Not observed live: a hypothesis from GitHub's public documentation and three public third-party reports, filed before the sixth (B) spends a transfer on it. Activation step 5 (25a row 7: brain/integration is cut from main) is one call, POST /repos/{repo}/git/refs {ref: refs/heads/brain/integration, sha: <main's head>}. 25a row 3 asks a ruleset on brain/integration with a required status check (snowball-gate, strict, integration_id = the writer App). GitHub's REST page for repository rules (docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules, rule required_status_checks) gives that rule a parameter do_not_enforce_on_create: 'Allow repositories and branches to be created if a check would otherwise prohibit it', default false. Reports of the same call refused when the parameter is false, the branch cut at an existing commit of the default branch that carries no run of the required check: github.com/ghanbak/sw-books/issues/113 ('POST /git/refs returned 422 with Reference update failed', repaired by ticking 'Do not require status checks on creation'), github.com/orgs/community/discussions/112472 (same refusal, same repair). main's head in the toy and in the copy has no snowball-gate check run (the toy has no workflow, 25a row 6; the writer App posts that check only on candidate heads), so with the parameter false the cut would be answered 422. In the brain's code the cut is the first write of the genesis cycle (activate.py, the line the second grep prints), so that answer ends yaz red with nothing written to the target: no branch to archive, but a (B) attempt and a transfer spent, and no later step reached. My test world cannot show this: tests/fake_github.py refuses a creation only for a name a test puts in create_denied, and its docstring says GitHub's answer there is not modelled as known. What the seed does not say: no page names do_not_enforce_on_create (grep above: no line); 25a row 3 lists the required check without it, and 29o's closed list of genesis reasons has none for a ruleset that would refuse the cut, though GET rules/branches/brain/integration, which genesis already reads, carries the parameter in the rule's parameters. Asked of the operator: (1) before the next transfer, read the brain/integration ruleset of both targets and set 'Do not require status checks on creation' (do_not_enforce_on_create: true) if it is not set, or say that the cut is made another way; (2) a line in 25a row 3 naming the parameter, with the two other values the writer's calls need of that ruleset's pull_request rule: required_approving_review_count 0 and allowed_merge_methods holding merge (the writer sends merge_method: merge, 29i); (3) if genesis should refuse instead of the cut failing, a reason in 29o's list and a vector for it (the list is closed by the genesis vectors, so the brain cannot add one). A second thing read on the same page and left as a question, not a finding: for an expected check tied to an App it says the App 'must be installed in the repository with the statuses:write permission', while 25 item 6 gives the writer App checks:write and the writer posts a check run; whether a check run by an App without statuses:write satisfies the rule is not something a session can see.
